bifrost: springboard/ui/src/transcript.rs, springboard/ui/src/context_window.rs, springboard/ui/src/generation_schema.rs (pure models), springboard/apps/assistant-desktop (cloud Anthropic client), springboard/sdk/src/url.rs (streaming), springboard/sdk/src/intents.rs (App Intents)
summary: Apple's framework runs an on-device language model (SystemLanguageModel) with sessions, guided generation, tool calling and an optional Private Cloud Compute model. BifrOSt has no on-device model, no SDK API for model sessions and no model-invoked tools. Pure models now cover transcripts, a context window budget and schema checks of structured output (springboard/ui/src), so those three rows are partial; the Assistant is still a cloud client.

features.note: no local model runtime in the SDK or the shell; springboard/apps/assistant-desktop/src/model.rs DEFAULT_MODEL is a cloud model id
the Assistant builds Messages API requests by hand; no reusable session type in bifrost_app
HTTP byte streaming exists for the Assistant's SSE; no model-level partial-generation API

a schema of typed, described members with choices and numeric ranges, and a check of a returned value that reports every problem; nothing constrains the model while it writes, and there is no macro or typed decoding into generated values

features.apple: Tool protocol, tool calling in sessions
features.note: ToolCall and ToolOutput entries exist in the transcript model (springboard/ui/src/transcript.rs); no model invokes a tool yet, so the status stays gap

features.apple: App Intents overlap (Apple exposes intents separately from Foundation Models)
features.note: typed intents with parameters and shortcuts exist; they could later serve as tool definitions

a character-based estimate of about four characters per token, not a model tokenizer; fit keeps the instructions and the newest turns that fit, starting at a prompt; no cached-state reuse across turns

features.apple: Transcripts, transcript entries, segments and attachments
features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/transcript.rs (Transcript, Entry, Segment, Structured), springboard/apps/assistant-desktop/src/model.rs (conversations as JSON files)
features.note: a typed transcript with a leading instructions entry kept apart from the history, text, and typed lists of tool calls, tool outputs and responses; the Assistant still keeps its own store and no transcript is shared across apps
images can be decoded, but the Assistant has no image input path to a model
the Assistant is hard-wired to the Anthropic Messages API

features.apple: Improving the safety of generative model output (guidance, guardrail errors)
features.note: no output filtering in the SDK

features.apple: Content tagging (topics, actions, objects, emotions) in SystemLanguageModel
features.note: pattern-based data detectors for links, dates and addresses; no model-based tagging of topics or emotions
Apple-hosted service and entitlement with no BifrOSt counterpart

features.feature: Evaluation and runtime profiling of prompts
features.apple: Evaluating prompts, evaluating responses, Instruments profiling
features.note: benchmarks and logs exist for the shell; nothing measures prompts or model responses

gaps: No on-device language model and no SDK API for it: an app cannot ask the system for text generation without a network call.
No model session type with instructions, prompts, generation options and streamed partial output.
Guided generation is validation only: no model output is constrained to a typed schema, and there is no typed decoding into generated values.
No model-invoked tool calling; App Intents (springboard/sdk/src/intents.rs) exist but are not exposed to a model.
The context budget is a character estimate: there is no model tokenizer, and no cached state is reused across turns.
Transcripts exist as a pure model (springboard/ui/src/transcript.rs) but are not shared across apps; the Assistant keeps its own store.
The Assistant (springboard/apps/assistant-desktop) is a cloud client for the Anthropic API, not an on-device or Apple-equivalent feature, so it does not count as parity.
